title: V_eta migration coverage ledger
description: One row per did_v1 SOURCE class, from BOTH v1 writers: the NDI production templates (read from NDI-matlab `origin/main`, not a lagging feature branch) AND the vhlab app/calculator classes that appear in real corpora but ship no NDI template (footprint = a bespoke migrator that consumes them). rows.how: KEEPS ITS CLASS -- a block FOLD, not a dissolution. `oneepoch` is the record of a CONCATENATION (ndi.element.oneepoch glues an element's N epochs into one); its only own field, `epoch_ids`, is the comma-joined list of the sources. Everything else arrives by inheritance from `element_epoch`, which V_eta renames to `acquisition_epoch` -- so no class of that name exists to inherit from and the inherited block would trip the strict top-level check (did2:validation:undeclaredBlock). The migrator moves that block's contents onto the `oneepoch` block and drops the shell. Field-by-field, so an unrecognised v1 field surfaces as undeclaredField rather than riding along unvalidated.
rows.target_flags: PASSTHROUGH REPAIR, NOT THE MODEL. Before this the class had NO V_eta schema at all -- coverage.py tagged it non-production, which suppressed the gap -- and a real document quarantined on `No schema file for class "oneepoch"` (measured: DID-matlab scratch probe 8, run 31423494433). The go-forward model is fork A1, chosen by the team 2026-08-10 and recorded in V_eta_epoch_plan.md: the concatenation becomes a typed observation whose `derived_from_#` edges point at the N per-epoch observations, and NO `epoch` entity is minted for the synthetic `whole_session_<ref>` id. That build is gated on the raw-recording plan being signed. NOTE the tombstone declares `clocks`, NOT the did_v1 `epoch_clock`/`t0_t1`: the base element_epoch superclass migrator collapses the pair before validation sees the document, so the did_v1 names never arrive.

rows.how: NO PASS-1 MIGRATOR, deliberately: the document passes through under its own tombstone (the identity migrator), which is what stops it stranding. The GO-FORWARD fact is minted in the SECOND PASS -- did2.convert.resolveValidIntervals -- which decomposes the v1 ARRAY block into ONE `validity_observation` per interval (subject_id = the element_id the writer set, ids preserved by migrators_j.element's promotion; boolean value TRUE; `sequence` = the v1 array-append position, because tuning_response.m reads the FIRST interval only) plus the `relative_reference` each statement is anchored to (start = t0, duration = t1 - t0, clock de-encoded from clocktypestring). A batch pass and not a migrator for the same structural reason as resolveSessionAnchors: `relative_reference.relative_to` is REQUIRED and names the `epoch` DOCUMENT, whose id exists only after did2.convert.epochMint has minted it corpus-wide, and a single-document migrator holds an epoch STRING it cannot map to a document id.
